target: Caso ele ligue, avisa pra mim.
english: If he calls, let me know.
tip: 'Caso' meaning if or in case forces the subjunctive: ligue, not liga.

target: Nos abraçamos e nos despedimos.
english: We hugged each other and said farewell.
tip: Here 'nos' means each other, not ourselves: nos abraçamos is we hugged one another.

target: Vocês se acostumaram com o calor?
english: Did you get used to the heat?
tip: Acostumar-se pairs with com to mark what you get used to: se acostumaram com o calor, got used to the heat.

target: Eu preciso terminar isso para amanhã.
english: I need to finish this by tomorrow.
tip: 'Para' with a time marks a deadline, meaning by: para amanhã is by tomorrow, not for tomorrow.

target: Não há ninguém que saiba disso.
english: There's no one who knows about this.
tip: When the person you describe doesn't exist, the verb goes subjunctive: ninguém que saiba, 'no one who knows'.

target: Por que ele não respondeu a mensagem?
english: Why didn't he respond to the message?
tip: In a question it stays two words, por que; the one-word porque means because and belongs in the answer.

target: Embora a comida esteja fria, está gostosa.
english: Although the food is cold, it's tasty.
tip: 'Embora' (although) always requires the subjunctive – it introduces a concession.

target: Chovia muito quando a gente chegou.
english: It was raining a lot when we arrived.
tip: Imperfeito 'chovia' sets the ongoing background, while preterite chegou marks the single event that cut in.

target: Não quero que ninguém saiba disso.
english: I don't want anyone to know about this.
tip: 'Querer que' always triggers the subjunctive – whenever one person wants another to do something.

target: Para mim, café é essencial de manhã.
english: For me, coffee is essential in the morning.
tip: 'Para mim' = for me (opinion/benefit). Don't confuse with 'por mim' = as far as I'm concerned / on my behalf.

target: O show já tinha começado quando nós chegamos.
english: The show had already started when we arrived.
tip: 'Tinha' plus a participle is the pluperfect, an action done before another past event: tinha começado, had started.

target: Eu me mudei para São Paulo há dois anos.
english: I moved to São Paulo two years ago.
tip: 'Há' plus a time span means ago: há dois anos is two years ago. Note the spelling há, not a.

target: Enquanto eu falava, ela anotava tudo.
english: While I was talking, she was writing everything down.
tip: Two simultaneous ongoing actions both use imperfeito: 'falava' and 'anotava' were happening at the same time.

target: Obrigado por tudo.
english: Thank you for everything.
tip: 'Obrigado por' = thank you for. Use 'por' when thanking someone for something they already did. It's about the reason for your gratitude.

target: Ela se demitiu do emprego.
english: She quit her job.
tip: Demitir-se means to quit your own job. Drop the se and demitir means to fire someone. Ela se demitiu = she resigned.

target: Fala mais devagar, por favor.
english: Speak more slowly, please.
tip: In casual Brazilian Portuguese the command uses the ele form: fala, not the textbook fale. Fala mais devagar = speak more slowly.

target: Eu me cortei fazendo a barba.
english: I cut myself shaving.
tip: Fazer a barba literally means to make the beard, but it is the normal way to say to shave. Eu me cortei fazendo a barba = I cut myself shaving.

target: Nós nos demos conta do erro.
english: We realized the mistake.
tip: Dar-se conta de is a set phrase for to realize or become aware. Nós nos demos conta do erro = we realized the mistake.

target: A gente se comunica pelo WhatsApp.
english: We communicate through WhatsApp.
tip: A gente means we in casual speech but takes a singular verb like ele. That is why it is se comunica, never comunicam.

target: Ela lutou por seus direitos.
english: She fought for her rights.
tip: 'Por' for 'on behalf of' or 'in defense of': 'lutar por' = to fight for, 'votar por' = to vote for.

target: Ele foi preso por roubo.
english: He was arrested for robbery.
tip: Foi preso is passive: ser plus a past participle. Preso agrees with the subject, so a woman would be foi presa.

target: Eu não o conheço pessoalmente.
english: I don't know him personally.
tip: The o before conheço means him, a direct object pronoun sitting in front of the verb. In speech many say não conheço ele instead.

target: Vocês se lembram do aniversário dele?
english: Do you remember his birthday?
tip: 'Lembrar-se de' means 'to remember.' The 'se' makes it reflexive. You can also say 'lembrar de' without 'se' – both are correct in Brazil.

target: Eu me apaixonei pelo Brasil.
english: I fell in love with Brazil.
tip: Apaixonar-se takes por for what you fall for, and por plus o contracts to pelo. Eu me apaixonei pelo Brasil = I fell in love with Brazil.

target: Para quando você precisa disso?
english: When do you need this?
tip: 'Para' for deadlines: 'para quando' = by when, 'para amanhã' = by tomorrow, 'para sexta' = by Friday.

target: Nós nos casamos há cinco anos.
english: We got married five years ago.
tip: Há plus a length of time means ago: há cinco anos = five years ago. It comes from haver, not from ter.

target: Eu fiz isso para ajudar você.
english: I did this to help you.
tip: para plus an infinitive states purpose, the why: para ajudar means 'in order to help'.

target: Vocês se divertiram na festa?
english: Did you have fun at the party?
tip: Divertir-se is reflexive in Portuguese: você se diverte to have fun. Vocês se divertiram na festa = did you enjoy the party.

target: Nós nos conhecemos numa festa.
english: We met each other at a party.
tip: Conhecer usually means to know, but with the reciprocal nos it means to meet for the first time. Nós nos conhecemos numa festa = we met at a party.

target: Para ser sincero, eu não gostei.
english: To be honest, I didn't like it.
tip: Gostar normally needs de before its object, but when the thing is already clear you can drop it: não gostei = I didn't like it.
